title: refactor: simplify app management and deployments
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Moves the unchanged 882-row community catalog and its ingestion, validation, metrics, and Tinybird sync code to `operations/app-management/` as `app.json` and `app.js`.
- Leaves `apps/` for application directories only; removes obsolete generated listings, templates, and stale deployment guides.
- Replaces central deployment registries and three workflows with per-application `deploy.json` manifests and one production-only deployment engine.
- Catalog-only and deployment-engine-only changes do not trigger application deployments.
- Tinybird changes are descriptive only; no schema, SQL, or endpoint behavior changes.

Rollout:
- Merge requires an immediate main→production sync and website deploy because the live bundle reads the catalog from `main` at runtime.
- The first production sync adds all 20 manifests and therefore deploys all 20 applications; monitor that run. Future engine-only edits deploy none.

Checks:
- 11 tests pass
- Catalog validates with 882 byte-identical rows
- Workflow YAML, shell syntax, and diff checks pass

gist.headline: One hive, fewer levers
gist.blurb: App deployments have stopped consulting several ancient scrolls. Each app now carries its own small deployment manifest, while one engine handles the actual gardening.
gist.summary: Replaced central deployment registries and three deployment workflows with per-app deploy.json manifests for 20 applications and a single production deployment engine, while moving the unchanged 882-entry community catalog into operations/app-management.
gist.impact: Application directories are now cleaner and deployment changes are more targeted: catalog-only or deployment-engine-only edits do not redeploy apps, while each app declares its own deployment configuration beside its code.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden keeper replacing a tangled wall of old deployment maps and switches with neat labeled seed packets, one beside each tiny app-shaped planter. A friendly CRT monitor robot can help organize the manifests, with a cozy app garden and a single glowing deployment watering system representing the unified engine.
